newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares edged up to their third closing high this month but prices eased in late trading as the psychologically important 700 point level beckoned.
The AEX index of 30 leading shares closed at 695.04 points, a gain of just 0.79 on the day, after earlier hitting an intra record peak of 698.21.
Dealers said futures-related selling and an easing of shares on Wall Street undermined the Dutch index in the last hour as it was heading toward 700.
"The market might have some problems with round numbers. Chartists call it 'roundaphobia'," one dealer said.
He noted profit-taking in Royal Dutch Petroleum, which ended 2.90 guilders lower at 333.70, and brewer Heineken, whose close of 315.20 guilders was 4.80 down on Friday's level.
The lower oil price also weighed down on Royal Dutch, as did the fall in Far East trading of the dollar in the wake of Saturday's G7 meeting, which undermined other global stocks.
Philips Electronics lost 0.10 to 74.70 but consumer products giant Unilever bucked the trend among international Dutch stocks, ending up 3.10 to 313.40.
Royal Dutch, Unilever and Philips are among the companies reporting results this week, kicking off the reporting season.
Computer software producer Baan added 0.80 to close at 86.30 guilders after Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to its recommended list from a market outperform category.
Construction firm Volker Stevin was another big gainer, closing 6.50 higher at 190.00 guilders on news of its planned four-for-one share split.

But the biggest loser of the day was cable maker NKF Holding, whose shares dived 17.50 to 56.00 guilders, a loss of 24 percent after warning it expected 1997 profits to be substantially below those of 1996.
"It was a huge fall," commented one trader.
In line with the firmer Dutch bond market, financial stocks were mainly stronger.
Options traders reported switching into call options of ABN AMRO and ING Groep from the underlying shares.

Technical analysts changed their recent neutral view on the AEX index to a positive one in response to last week's 18.57 point rise, setting an initial target of 700 points with the second resistance level seen between 715 and 720.
One dealer said: "The market is in very good shape."
But another dealer said buyers may wait for a correction before stepping back in again.
